passage:
Indu: he said “is your brain on holiday” in front of everyone
Ishita: I know, I was there. I'm sorry. The whole room went so quiet
Indu: I wanted to disappear
Ishita: what happened after class?
Indu: Sir, our maths teacher, asked me to stay back. He said he'd spoken sharply, it wasn't fair, and my second step was right
Ishita: really??
Indu: and he said he'd say something to the class tomorrow too
(Next day)
Indu: he did. He said “Yesterday I mocked an answer. That's not how we work in this room. We ask, we fix, we don't label.” He didn't say my name
Ishita: the back row stopped smirking
Indu: it still stings a bit. but better

qa.q: What did the teacher say in front of everyone that Indu quotes at the start?
qa.a: He said, “is your brain on holiday” in front of everyone.

qa.q: How did Indu feel during the incident, and what shows it?
qa.a: Indu wanted to disappear, which shows in “I wanted to disappear,” and still felt a sting the next day, though a bit better.

qa.q: Why did it help that the teacher spoke privately first and then spoke to the class without naming Indu?
qa.a: The private words repaired the hurt to Indu, and the class talk set a norm without shaming anyone, so neither Indu nor the class was made a target.

qa.q: How might Ishita have seen the class talk the next day?
qa.a: Ishita seems to have felt relief, since Ishita noticed that the back row stopped smirking after the teacher spoke.

grounding: After a humiliating moment, a teacher speaks privately with the student and then addresses the class norm without shaming anyone.

passage: In the small-town school's lab, Tushar's elbow knocked a glass beaker off the bench. It shattered. “Are you stupid?” the science teacher snapped, and half the class laughed. Tushar's ears burned. Ishita, at the next bench, stopped writing. The next morning the teacher called Tushar to the veranda before assembly. “I spoke to you in a way I shouldn't have,” the teacher said. “A beaker costs little. I'm sorry.” Tushar nodded, unsure what to say. Later, in class, the teacher told everyone, “Yesterday some of us laughed at a mistake. In this lab we clear up together, and nobody is laughed at.” Ishita went to fetch the dustpan, and three others followed.

qa.q: Where did the teacher take Tushar the next morning?
qa.a: The teacher called Tushar to the veranda before assembly.

qa.q: What might Tushar have been feeling when Tushar nodded, unsure what to say?
qa.a: Tushar probably felt a mix of relief and awkwardness after the humiliation, and did not know how to answer an adult's apology.

qa.q: What did the teacher do to repair the moment?
qa.a: The teacher apologised privately for the tone, then told the class that nobody is laughed at in the lab and that clearing up is done together, without naming or shaming anyone.

qa.q: Why might Ishita have gone to fetch the dustpan first?
qa.a: Ishita had stopped writing when the beaker broke and seems to have wanted to show that helping, not laughing, is the norm, and three others followed.

grounding: After a humiliating moment, a teacher speaks privately to the student and then sets a class norm without shaming anyone.
